title: Arakhin 16
description: Speech said before three, praise that turns into a curse, the seven sins that bring leprous marks and the priestly vestments that atone, why the leper dwells alone, and the duty of rebuke, with a guest’s lodging, a craftsman’s trade and the smallest measure of suffering.
topics: 🗣️ Said before three: “your friend has a friend”
🍞 Praise that turns into a curse: the grateful guest, and Rav Dimi’s sickbed
⚪ Seven sins that bring leprous marks, each with its verse
👘 What each priestly vestment atones for, and the robe, the incense and the heifer
🐦 Why the leper dwells alone and brings chirping birds
🗨️ Rebuke: rebuking again, who can take it, who knows how to give it, and how far it goes
🏠 Not changing one’s lodging or one’s family craft
🧺 The smallest measure of suffering, and forty days without it

a1.he: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: כֹּל מִילְּתָא דְּמִיתְאַמְרָא בְּאַפֵּי תְּלָתָא, לֵית בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם לִישָּׁנָא בִּישָׁא. מַאי טַעְמָא? חַבְרָךְ חַבְרָא אִית לֵיהּ, וְחַבְרָא דְּחַבְרָךְ חַבְרָא אִית לֵיהּ.

a2.he: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״מְבָרֵךְ רֵעֵהוּ בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל בַּבּוֹקֶר הַשְׁכֵּם קְלָלָה תֵּחָשֵׁב לוֹ״? כְּגוֹן דְּמִיקְּלַע לְאוּשְׁפִּיזָא וְטָרְחוּ קַמֵּיהּ שַׁפִּיר, לִמְחַר נָפֵיק יָתֵיב בְּשׁוּקָא וְאָמַר: רַחֲמָנָא נִיבָרְכֵיהּ לִפְלָנְיָא דְּהָכִי טְרַח קַמַּאי, וְשָׁמְעִין אִינָשֵׁי וְאָזְלִין וְאָנְסִין לֵיהּ.

a3.he: תָּנֵי רַב דִּימִי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סָפְרָא: לְעוֹלָם אַל יְסַפֵּר אָדָם בְּטוֹבָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ טוֹבָתוֹ בָּא לִידֵי רָעָתוֹ.

a4.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַב דִּימִי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סָפְרָא חֲלַשׁ, עָל רַב סָפְרָא לְשַׁיּוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ. אֲמַר לְהוּ: תֵּיתֵי לִי דְּקַיֵּימִי כֹּל דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא מִי מְקַיְּימַתְּ — לְעוֹלָם אַל יְסַפֵּר אָדָם בְּטוֹבָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ טוֹבָתוֹ בָּא לִידֵי גְּנוּתוֹ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא שְׁמִיעָא לִי, וְאִי הֲוָה שְׁמִיעָא לִי — קַיֵּימְתַּהּ.

a5.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עַל שִׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים נְגָעִים בָּאִין — עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, וְעַל שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, וְעַל שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא, וְעַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וְעַל גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ, וְעַל הַגָּזֵל, וְעַל צָרוּת הָעַיִן.

a6.he: עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע — דִּכְתִיב: ״מְלׇשְׁנִי בַסֵּתֶר רֵעֵהוּ אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית״.

a7.he: עַל שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים — דִּכְתִיב ״וְאַל יִכָּרֵת מִבֵּית יוֹאָב זָב וּמְצֹרָע וְגוֹ׳״.

a8.he: וְעַל שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא — דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר נַעֲמָן הוֹאֵל קַח כִּכָּרָיִם״, וּכְתִיב: ״וְצָרַעַת נַעֲמָן תִּדְבַּק בְּךָ וְגוֹ׳״.

a9.he: וְעַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת — דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְנַגַּע ה׳ אֶת פַּרְעֹה נְגָעִים וְגוֹ׳״.

a10.he: וְעַל גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ — דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְחֶזְקָתוֹ גָּבַהּ לִבּוֹ עַד לְהַשְׁחִית וַיִּמְעוֹל בַּה׳ אֱלֹהָיו״, ״וְהַצָּרַעַת זָרְחָה בְּמִצְחוֹ״.

a11.he: וְעַל הַגָּזֵל — דִּכְתִיב: ״וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן וּפִנּוּ אֶת הַבַּיִת״. תָּנָא: הוּא כּוֹנֵס מָמוֹן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ, יָבֹא הַכֹּהֵן וִיפַזֵּר מָמוֹנוֹ.

a12.he: וְעַל צָרוּת הָעַיִן — דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבָא אֲשֶׁר לוֹ הַבַּיִת״, וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: מִי שֶׁמְיוּחָד בֵּיתוֹ לוֹ.

a13.he: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי עֲנָנִי בַּר שָׂשׂוֹן: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת בִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה לְפָרָשַׁת קׇרְבָּנוֹת? לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה קׇרְבָּנוֹת מְכַפְּרִין — אַף בִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה מְכַפְּרִין. כְּתוֹנֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּטְבְּלוּ אֶת הַכֻּתֹּנֶת בַּדָּם״. מִכְנָסַיִם מְכַפְּרִים עַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַעֲשֵׂה לָהֶם מִכְנְסֵי בָד לְכַסּוֹת בְּשַׂר עֶרְוָה״.

a14.he: מִצְנֶפֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל גַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ — כִּדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: יָבֹא דָּבָר שֶׁבַּגּוֹבַהּ וִיכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה גּוֹבַהּ. אַבְנֵט (מכפרת) [מְכַפֵּר] עַל הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב, אַהֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהָיָה עַל לֵב אַהֲרֹן״.

a15.he: חוֹשֶׁן מְכַפֵּר עַל הַדִּינִין — דִּכְתִיב: ״וְעָשִׂיתָ חֹשֶׁן מִשְׁפָּט״. אֵפוֹד מְכַפֵּר עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״אֵין אֵפוֹד וּתְרָפִים״. מְעִיל מְכַפֵּר עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: יָבֹא דָּבָר שֶׁבַּקּוֹל וִיכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַקּוֹל.

a16.he: צִיץ מְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עַזֵּי פָנִים — כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וְהָיָה עַל מֵצַח אַהֲרֹן״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וּמֵצַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה הָיָה לָךְ״.

a17.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאַהֲנוֹ מַעֲשָׂיו, הָא דְּלָא אַהֲנוֹ מַעֲשָׂיו. אִי אַהֲנוֹ מַעֲשָׂיו — אָתוּ נְגָעִים עֲלֵיהּ, אִי לָא אַהֲנוֹ מַעֲשָׂיו — מְעִיל מְכַפֵּר.

a18.he: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי סִימוֹן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים לֹא מָצִינוּ לָהֶם בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת כַּפָּרָה, בְּדָבָר אַחֵר מָצִינוּ לָהֶם כַּפָּרָה, שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע. שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים בְּעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה.

a19.he: וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע — בִּקְטֹרֶת, דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לָמַדְנוּ לִקְטֹרֶת שֶׁמְּכַפֶּרֶת, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּתֵּן אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת וַיְכַפֵּר עַל הָעָם״, וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: עַל מָה קְטֹרֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת — עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: יָבֹא דָּבָר שֶׁבַּחֲשַׁאי וִיכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה חֲשַׁאי.

a20.he: קַשְׁיָא שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים אַשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, קַשְׁיָא לָשׁוֹן הָרָע אַלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע!

a21.he: שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים אַשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דִּידִיעַ מַאן קַטְלֵיהּ, הָא דְּלָא יְדִיעַ מַאן קַטְלֵיהּ.

a22.he: דִּידִיעַ מַאן קַטְלֵיהּ בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא! בְּמֵזִיד וְלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ.

a23.he: לָשׁוֹן הָרָע אַלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּצִינְעָא,

b2.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נָדָב מֵרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נָדָב חַתְנֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מֵרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מֵרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מָה נִשְׁתַּנָּה מְצוֹרָע שֶׁאָמְרָה תּוֹרָה ״בָּדָד יֵשֵׁב מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה מוֹשָׁבוֹ״? הוּא הִבְדִּיל בֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ, בֵּין אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ, לְפִיכָךְ אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה ״בָּדָד יֵשֵׁב וְגוֹ׳״.

b3.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לֵוִי: מָה נִשְׁתַּנָּה מְצוֹרָע שֶׁאָמְרָה תּוֹרָה יָבִיא שְׁתֵּי צִיפֳּרִים לְטׇהֳרָתוֹ? אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: הוּא עוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֵׂה פַּטִּיט, לְפִיכָךְ אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה יָבִיא קׇרְבַּן פַּטִּיט.

b4.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״לֹא תִשְׂנָא אֶת אָחִיךָ בִּלְבָבֶךָ״ — יָכוֹל לֹא יַכֶּנּוּ, לֹא יִסְטְרֶנּוּ, וְלֹא יְקַלְּלֶנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בִּלְבָבֶךָ״ — שִׂנְאָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.

b5.he: מִנַּיִן לָרוֹאֶה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ דָּבָר מְגוּנֶּה שֶׁחַיָּיב לְהוֹכִיחוֹ? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הוֹכֵחַ תּוֹכִיחַ״. הוֹכִיחוֹ וְלֹא קִבֵּל, מִנַּיִן שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר וְיוֹכִיחֶנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תּוֹכִיחַ״, מִכׇּל מָקוֹם. יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ מִשְׁתַּנִּים פָּנָיו? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לֹא תִשָּׂא עָלָיו חֵטְא״.

b6.he: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: תְּמֵיהַנִי אֲנִי אִם יֵשׁ בַּדּוֹר הַזֶּה שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל תּוֹכֵחָה, אֲפִילּוּ אָמַר לוֹ ״טוֹל קֵיסָם מִבֵּין עֵינֶיךָ״, אוֹמֵר לוֹ ״טוֹל קוֹרָה מִבֵּין עֵינֶיךָ״. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: תְּמֵיהַנִי אִם יֵשׁ בְּדוֹר הַזֶּה שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לְהוֹכִיחַ.

b7.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי: מֵעִיד אֲנִי עָלַי שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ שֶׁהַרְבֵּה פְּעָמִים לָקָה עֲקִיבָא עַל יְדֵי, שֶׁהָיִיתִי קוֹבֵל עָלָיו לִפְנֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרִיבִּי, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁהוֹסַפְתִּי בּוֹ אַהֲבָה, לְקַיֵּים מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַל תּוֹכַח לֵץ פֶּן יִשְׂנָאֶךָּ הוֹכַח לְחָכָם וְיֶאֱהָבֶךָּ״.

b8.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: תּוֹכֵחָה לִשְׁמָהּ וַעֲנָוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ עֲדִיפָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלָא מוֹדֵית דַּעֲנָוָה לִשְׁמָהּ עֲדִיפָא, דְּאָמַר מָר: עֲנָוָה גְּדוֹלָה מִכּוּלָּם? שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ נָמֵי עֲדִיפָא, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק אָדָם בְּתוֹרָה וּבְמִצְוֹת אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ בָּא לִשְׁמָהּ.

b9.he: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי תּוֹכֵחָה לִשְׁמָהּ וַעֲנָוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ? כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲמַר לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב: חֲזִי מָר דְּקָא מְצַעַר לִי. קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ דְּתוּ לָא מְצַעַר לֵיהּ. בָּתַר דְּנָפֵיק, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי וְהָכִי קָא עָבֵיד. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לֵיהּ בְּאַנְפֵּיהּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַס לִי דְּלִיכְּסִיף זַרְעֵיהּ דְּרַב עַל יְדַאי!

b10.he: עַד הֵיכָן תּוֹכֵחָה? רַב אָמַר: עַד הַכָּאָה, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עַד קְלָלָה, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: עַד נְזִיפָה. כְּתַנָּאֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עַד הַכָּאָה, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: עַד קְלָלָה, בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: עַד נְזִיפָה.

b11.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וּשְׁלׇשְׁתָּן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ: ״וַיִּחַר אַף שָׁאוּל בִּיהוֹנָתָן וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ בֶּן נַעֲוַת הַמַּרְדּוּת״, וּכְתִיב: ״וַיָּטֶל שָׁאוּל אֶת הַחֲנִית עָלָיו לְהַכּוֹתוֹ״.

b12.he: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַד הַכָּאָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״לְהַכּוֹתוֹ״, וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַד קְלָלָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״לְבׇשְׁתְּךָ וּלְבֹשֶׁת עֶרְוַת אִמֶּךָ״, וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַד נְזִיפָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּחַר אַף שָׁאוּל״.

b13.he: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר נְזִיפָה, הָכְתִיב הַכָּאָה וּקְלָלָה! שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאַגַּב חַבִּיבוּתָא יַתִּירָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּיהּ לִיהוֹנָתָן בְּדָוִד, מְסַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ טְפֵי.

b14.he: עַד הֵיכָן לֹא יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם בָּאַכְסַנְיָא שֶׁלּוֹ? רַב אָמַר: עַד הַכָּאָה, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עַד שֶׁיַּפְשִׁלוּ לוֹ כֵּלָיו לַאֲחוֹרָיו.

b15.he: בְּהַכָּאָה דִּידֵיהּ — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי, בְּהַפְשָׁלַת כֵּלָיו לַאֲחוֹרָיו — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא נָמֵי לָא פְּלִיגִי, כִּי פְּלִיגִי — בְּהַכָּאָה דִּדְבֵיתְהוּ, מָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דִּלְדִידֵיהּ לָא מְצַעֵר לֵיהּ מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינַּהּ, וּמָר סָבַר: אָתֵי לְאִיטְּרוֹדֵי.

b16.he: וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה? דְּאָמַר מָר: אַכְסְנַאי פּוֹגֵם וְנִפְגָּם.

b17.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם בָּאַכְסַנְיָא שֶׁלּוֹ מִן הַתּוֹרָה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר הָיָה שָׁם אׇהֳלוֹ בַּתְּחִלָּה״.

b18.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר, מֵהָכָא ״וַיֵּלֶךְ לְמַסָּעָיו״. מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ אַכְסְנַאי דְּאַקְרַאי.

b19.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם מֵאוּמָּנוּתוֹ וּמֵאוּמָּנוּת אֲבוֹתָיו? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּשְׁלַח הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה וַיִּקַּח אֶת חִירָם מִצֹּר, בֶּן אִשָּׁה אַלְמָנָה הוּא מִמַּטֵּה נַפְתָּלִי וְאָבִיו אִישׁ צֹרִי חֹרֵשׁ נְחוֹשֶׁת״.

b20.he: וְאָמַר מָר: אִימֵּיהּ מִבֵּית דָּן, וּכְתִיב: ״וְאִתּוֹ אׇהֳלִיאָב בֶּן אֲחִיסָמָךְ לְמַטֵּה דָן״.

b21.he: עַד הֵיכָן תַּכְלִית יִסּוּרִין? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל שֶׁאָרְגוּ לוֹ בֶּגֶד לִלְבּוֹשׁ וְאֵין מִתְקַבֵּל עָלָיו. מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא זְעֵירָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי: גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ אָמְרוּ, אֲפִילּוּ נִתְכַּוְּונוּ לִמְזוֹג בְּחַמִּין וּמָזְגוּ לוֹ בְּצוֹנֵן, בְּצוֹנֵן וּמָזְגוּ לוֹ בְּחַמִּין, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ כּוּלֵּי הַאי?

b22.he: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נֶהְפַּךְ לוֹ חֲלוּקוֹ. רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: אֲפִילּוּ הוֹשִׁיט יָדוֹ לַכִּיס לִיטּוֹל שָׁלֹשׁ וְעָלוּ בְּיָדוֹ שְׁתַּיִם.

b23.he: דַּוְוקָא שָׁלֹשׁ וְעָלוּ בְּיָדוֹ שְׁתַּיִם, אֲבָל שְׁתַּיִם וְעָלוּ בְּיָדוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ — לָא, דְּלֵיכָּא טִירְחָא לְמִישְׁדְּיַיהּוֹ.

b24.he: וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה? דְּתַנְיָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: כֹּל שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלָיו אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם בְּלֹא יִסּוּרִין קִיבֵּל עוֹלָמוֹ. בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִי:

messages.text: Continued from 15b: Rabba said that a statement made in the presence of the person it concerns is not malicious speech. Abaye objected that it is all the more so, impudence and malicious speech, and Rabba replied that he holds like Rabbi Yosei, who never said something and then turned around to look behind him. The last words of 15b open a further statement:
Any matter that was said in the presence of three people does not have the status of malicious speech if one subsequently repeats it.

notes.dh: כל מילתא דמיתאמרא באפי תלתא לית בה משום לישנא בישא
notes.he: פירוש כגון כה"ג דנורא בי פלוני דאיכא למישמע דלא אמרה משום לישנא בישא אבל אם הוא אמר דבר קנטור על חבירו אפילו היה אומרה בפניו אית ביה משום לישנא בישא:
notes.en: Any matter that was said in the presence of three has no malicious speech in it: that is, a matter like “There is fire at so-and-so’s home” [15b], which can be understood as not said as malicious speech. But if he said something provocative against his fellow, even if he said it in his presence, it is malicious speech.

messages.text: What is the reason? The reason is that your friend has a friend, and your friend’s friend has a friend. Once the information has been stated in the presence of three people, it can be assumed that it will spread and become public knowledge, as each person will tell someone else.

notes.he: שהבעלים אמרוה בפני ג' המגלה אותה אינו לשון הרע שזה גילה תחלה דעתו שאם מגלה אותו אינו חושש דמידע ידע דסופה להגלות דחברך חברא אית ליה וזה מגלה לחבירו וזה לחבירו עד שיודע:
notes.en: That was said in the presence of three: if the owner [of the information] said it before three, one who reveals it is not speaking malicious speech, since the owner showed his mind from the start that he does not mind if it is revealed. For he surely knew that it would end up revealed, as “your friend has a friend”: this one reveals it to his friend and that one to his friend, until it is known.

notes.he: שהאחד הראשון אומרה בפני ג' אם חזר וסיפרה אחד מהם אין בו משום לשון הרע שלדעת כן אומרו בפני ג' שאינו חושש אם יתפרסם הדבר דחברך וכו']:
notes.en: Any matter that was said in the presence of three: when the first one said it before three, if one of them goes back and tells it, there is no malicious speech in it, since he said it before three knowingly, not minding if the matter becomes public, as “your friend has a friend,” and so on.

messages.text: What is the meaning of that which is written: “He that blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him”?
messages.lead: When Rav Dimi came from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia he said:

verse.he: מְבָרֵךְ רֵעֵהוּ ׀ בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל בַּבֹּקֶר הַשְׁכֵּים קְלָלָה תֵּחָשֶׁב לוֹ׃
verse.en:
He who greets his fellow loudly early in the morning
Shall have it reckoned to him as a curse.

notes.dh: מברך רעהו בקול גדול וגו' קללה תחשב לו
notes.he: אותה ברכה קללה היא לו לחבירו:
notes.en: He that blesses his friend with a loud voice … it shall be counted a curse to him: that blessing is a curse to him, to his friend [the host].

messages.text: For example, when one is invited to a host, and they look after him very well. The following day the guest goes out and sits in the marketplace and says: May the Merciful One bless so-and-so, as this is how well he looked after me.

And all the people in the marketplace hear and go to this host and afflict him by expecting him to look after all of them in the same way, and he is compelled to spend his money on them. It turns out that the praise and blessing the guest lavished upon his host brought a curse upon him.

notes.he: אלמים שהוא עשיר ואזלי ואנסי ליה לממוניה. ל"א אנסי ליה שמתאכסנין אצלו אורחין עד שמכלין ממונו:
notes.en: And people hear: violent people hear that he is rich, and they go and extort his money. Another version: they afflict him, in that guests come to lodge with him until they use up his money.

notes.he: שילטונין:
notes.en: And people hear and afflict him: the authorities.

notes.he: שאומרים ודאי עשיר הוא הואיל והוא מוציא כ"כ:
notes.en: And they afflict him: for they say, he is surely rich, since he spends so much.

messages.text: A person should never speak about the goodness of another in the presence of others, as through speaking about his goodness he will come to speak about him in a derogatory manner, as he will eventually note the exceptions to his goodness, or his listeners will temper his praise by mentioning that individual’s bad qualities.
messages.lead: Similarly, Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra, teaches:

notes.he: שכשהוא מספר בטובתו יותר מדאי הוא עצמו אומר חוץ ממדה רעה זו שבו או אחרים שומעין שזה משבחו ואומרים הלא מדת כך וכך בידו:
notes.en: He will come to speak of him in a derogatory manner: for when he tells of his goodness too much, he himself says “except for this bad trait in him,” or others hear him praising and say, “But doesn’t he have such-and-such a trait?”

notes.he: שמדקדקין אחריו ואומרים לו אותו שאתה משבח [כ"כ] הלא שמענו שעשה כך וכך:
notes.en: For through his goodness he comes to speak of his bad side: for they look into him and say to him: The one you praise so much, didn’t we hear that he did such-and-such?

messages.text: There are those who say that Rav Dimi did not actually make this statement himself. Rather, the following incident occurred: Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra, was ill. Rav Safra went in to inquire about his condition.

notes.he: לאו מימרא איתמר אלא כי ההיא גוונא [הוא. להשבע]:
notes.en: There are those who say: it was not stated as a teaching, but there was an incident of this kind. [A note in the printed edition adds that a comment seems to belong further on, at “Be content [ho’el], take two talents,” explaining that ho’el means an oath: to swear.]

messages.text: I have blessing and merit coming to me, as I have fulfilled all of the statements that the Sages say.

@Rav Dimi, brother of Rav Safra But have you fulfilled the instruction of the Sages that a person should never speak about the goodness of another in the presence of others, as through speaking about his goodness he will come to speak about him in a derogatory manner?
I never heard this statement of the Sages, but had I heard it, I would have fulfilled it.

§ Leprous marks come and afflict a person for seven sinful matters: For malicious speech, for bloodshed, for an oath taken in vain, for forbidden sexual relations, for arrogance, for theft, and for stinginess.

notes.he: שצרה עינו באחרים ואינו מהנה שכיניו מכליו ע"י שאלה:
notes.en: Stinginess [literally, narrowness of the eye]: his eye is narrow toward others, and he does not let his neighbors benefit from his utensils by lending them.

messages.text: The Gemara explains the source for the claim that each of these seven sins is punishable with leprosy. For malicious speech one is punished, as it is written: “Whoever defames his neighbor in secret, I will destroy him; whoever is haughty of eye and proud of heart, I will not suffer him.” The Gemara explained above (15b) that this is referring to leprosy.

verse.he: (מלושני) [מְלׇשְׁנִי] בַסֵּתֶר ׀ רֵעֵהוּ אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית גְּבַהּ־עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵבָב אֹתוֹ לֹא אוּכָל׃
verse.en:
One who slanders a friend in secret I will destroy;
I cannot endure anyone haughty and proud.

notes.he: ואוקימנא לעיל דהיינו נגעים:
notes.en: Him I will destroy: and we established above [15b] that this means leprous marks.

messages.text: For bloodshed, as it is written about Joab, as punishment for murdering Abner: “And let there not fail from the house of Joab a zav, or a leper, or that leans on a staff, or that falls by the sword, or that lacks bread.”

verse.he: יָחֻלוּ עַל־רֹאשׁ יוֹאָב וְאֶל כׇּל־בֵּית אָבִיו וְאַל־יִכָּרֵת מִבֵּית יוֹאָב זָב וּמְצֹרָע וּמַחֲזִיק בַּפֶּלֶךְ וְנֹפֵל בַּחֶרֶב וַחֲסַר־לָחֶם׃
verse.en: May [the guilt] fall upon the head of Joab and all his father’s house. May the house of Joab never be without someone suffering from a discharge or an eruption, or a male who handles the spindle, or one slain by the sword, or one lacking bread.”—

notes.he: מפני שהרג את אבנר:
notes.en: Let there not fail from the house of Joab: because he killed Abner.

messages.text: And for an oath taken in vain, as it is written: “And Naaman said: Be content [ho’el], take two talents. And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garment, and laid them upon two of his servants; and they bore them before him.”

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר נַעֲמָן הוֹאֵל קַח כִּכָּרָיִם וַיִּפְרׇץ־בּוֹ וַיָּצַר כִּכְּרַיִם כֶּסֶף בִּשְׁנֵי חֲרִטִים וּשְׁתֵּי חֲלִפוֹת בְּגָדִים וַיִּתֵּן אֶל־שְׁנֵי נְעָרָיו וַיִּשְׂאוּ לְפָנָיו׃
verse.en: Naaman said, “Please take two talents.” He urged him, and he wrapped the two talents of silver in two bags and gave them, along with two changes of clothes, to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of him.

notes.he: השבע ששלחך אלישע וקח ככרים:
notes.en: Ho’el: swear that Elisha sent you, and take the talents.

messages.text: The Sages maintain that the term ho’el indicates an oath, and that Naaman requested of Gehazi, to whom this was stated, to take an oath that Elisha had sent him to accept gifts, which Elisha had not done, and Gehazi took the oath. When Elisha found out what Gehazi had done he cursed him, and so it is written: “The leprosy of Naaman shall stick to you and to your children forever. And he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow.”

verse.he: וְצָרַעַת נַעֲמָן תִּדְבַּק־בְּךָ וּבְזַרְעֲךָ לְעוֹלָם וַיֵּצֵא מִלְּפָנָיו מְצֹרָע כַּשָּׁלֶג׃
verse.en: Surely, the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your descendants forever.” And as [Gehazi] left his presence, he was snow-white with leprosy.

messages.text: And for forbidden sexual relations, as it is written: “And the Lord afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great afflictions because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.”

verse.he: וַיְנַגַּע יְהֹוָה ׀ אֶת־פַּרְעֹה נְגָעִים גְּדֹלִים וְאֶת־בֵּיתוֹ עַל־דְּבַר שָׂרַי אֵשֶׁת אַבְרָם׃
verse.en: But GOD afflicted Pharaoh and his household with mighty plagues on account of Sarai, the wife of Abram.

messages.text: And for arrogance, as it is written with regard to King Uzziah: “But when he was strong his heart became arrogant so that he did corruptly, and he trespassed against the Lord his God; for he went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.”

verse.he: וּכְחֶזְקָתוֹ גָּבַהּ לִבּוֹ עַד־לְהַשְׁחִית וַיִּמְעַל בַּיהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו וַיָּבֹא אֶל־הֵיכַל יְהֹוָה לְהַקְטִיר עַל־מִזְבַּח הַקְּטֹרֶת׃
verse.en: When he was strong, he grew so arrogant he acted corruptly: he trespassed against his God by entering the Temple of GOD to offer incense on the incense altar.

notes.he: בעוזיהו משתעי:
notes.en: But when he was strong his heart became arrogant, and so on: the passage speaks of Uzziah.

notes.he: גבי עוזיה כתוב. בדברי הימים כתיב (ד"ה א ה) ויוחנן הוליד [את] עזריה (הכהן) [הוא] אשר כיהן (בתוך) בבית אשר בנה (המלך) שלמה [בירושלים] וצ"ע למה כתיב עליו אשר כיהן יותר מן האחרים שהוא מונה שם כל כהנים גדולים אשר שמשו בבית ראשון והרי מונה לפניו כמה כהנים ולמה כתיב אשר כיהן גבי (עוזיה) [עזרי'] יותר מן האחרים וי"ל לפי שהוא הכניס עצמו להתווכח על הכהונה כשבא עוזיה יותר מן האחרים:
notes.en: But when he was strong his heart became arrogant, and so on: this is written of Uzziah. In Chronicles it is written: “And Johanan begot Azariah; he it is who served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem” (I Chronicles 5). This needs study: why is “who served as priest” written of him more than of the others? For it lists there all the High Priests who served in the First Temple, and it lists several priests before him; why then is “who served as priest” written of Azariah more than of the others? One can say: because when Uzziah came [to burn the incense], he put himself forward to contend for the priesthood more than the others [see II Chronicles 26:17–18].

messages.text: And it states: “Then Uzziah was angry; and he had a censer in his hand to burn incense; and while he was angry with the priests, the leprosy broke forth in his forehead.”

verse.he: וַיִּזְעַף עֻזִּיָּהוּ וּבְיָדוֹ מִקְטֶרֶת לְהַקְטִיר וּבְזַעְפּוֹ עִם־הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַצָּרַעַת זָרְחָה בְמִצְחוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּבֵית יְהֹוָה מֵעַל לְמִזְבַּח הַקְּטֹרֶת׃
verse.en: Uzziah, holding the censer and ready to burn incense, got angry; but as he got angry with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead in front of the priests in the House of GOD beside the incense altar.

messages.text: And for theft, as it is written: “And the priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest go in to see the mark, that all that is in the house not become impure; and afterward the priest shall go in to see the house.”

verse.he: וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן וּפִנּוּ אֶת־הַבַּיִת בְּטֶרֶם יָבֹא הַכֹּהֵן לִרְאוֹת אֶת־הַנֶּגַע וְלֹא יִטְמָא כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר בַּבָּיִת וְאַחַר כֵּן יָבֹא הַכֹּהֵן לִרְאוֹת אֶת־הַבָּיִת׃
verse.en: The priest shall order the house cleared before the priest enters to examine the plague, so that nothing in the house may become impure; after that the priest shall enter to examine the house.

messages.text: He gathered property that is not his, therefore let the priest come and scatter his property.
messages.lead: In explanation of this verse, the Sages taught:

messages.text: And for stinginess, as it is written: “Then he that owns the house shall come and tell the priest, saying: There seems to me to be as it were a mark in the house.”

verse.he: וּבָא אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ הַבַּיִת וְהִגִּיד לַכֹּהֵן לֵאמֹר כְּנֶגַע נִרְאָה לִי בַּבָּיִת׃
verse.en: the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, “Something like a plague has appeared upon my house.”

messages.text: The verse calls him the one who owns the house because it is referring to one who was stingy and treated his house as being exclusively his, and did not allow others to share his property.
messages.lead: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

notes.he: כלי תשמישו שלא השאילם לאחרים:
notes.en: Who treated his house as exclusively his: his household utensils, which he did not lend to others.

notes.he: שרוצה להנות יחידי מכל טוב שיש לו בביתו ואינו רוצה שיהנו אחרים עמו:
notes.en: One whose house is exclusively his: who wants to enjoy alone all the good he has in his house and does not want others to enjoy it with him.

messages.text: Is that so? Doesn’t Rabbi Anani bar Sason say:

Why was the passage in the Torah that discusses the priestly vestments (Leviticus 8) juxtaposed to the passage that discusses offerings (Leviticus, chapters 1–7)? To tell you that just as offerings atone, so too the priestly vestments atone.

notes.he: בפרשת ואתה תצוה נסמכה ענין המילואים לבגדי כהונה:
notes.en: Why was it juxtaposed, and so on: in the portion of Ve’ata Tetzaveh, the matter of the inauguration offerings is juxtaposed to the priestly vestments. [Rashi thus places the juxtaposition in Exodus 28–29, not in Leviticus as the English gloss on the daf has it.]

messages.text: For what does each garment atone? The tunic [ketonet] atones for bloodshed, as it is written with regard to Joseph’s brothers after they plotted to kill him: “And they killed a goat, and dipped the coat [ketonet] in the blood.”

verse.he: וַיִּקְחוּ אֶת־כְּתֹנֶת יוֹסֵף וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ שְׂעִיר עִזִּים וַיִּטְבְּלוּ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּנֶת בַּדָּם׃
verse.en: Then they took Joseph’s tunic, slaughtered a kid, and dipped the tunic in the blood.

notes.he: רמז היה להם שטבילת כפרת דמים עולה ע"י כתנת:
notes.en: And they dipped the coat in the blood: it was a hint for them that atonement for blood would come about through a tunic.

notes.he: סימן יבא כתנת ויכפר על מעשה דם:
notes.en: And they dipped the coat in the blood: a sign: let the tunic come and atone for an act of blood.

messages.text: The trousers atone for forbidden sexual relations, as it is written with regard to the priestly vestments: “And you shall make them linen trousers to cover the flesh of their nakedness.”

verse.he: וַעֲשֵׂה לָהֶם מִכְנְסֵי־בָד לְכַסּוֹת בְּשַׂר עֶרְוָה מִמׇּתְנַיִם וְעַד־יְרֵכַיִם יִהְיוּ׃
verse.en: You shall also make for them linen breeches to cover their nakedness; they shall extend from the hips to the thighs.

messages.text: The mitre atones for the arrogant, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ḥanina,
It is logical that an item placed at an elevation, i.e., on the head of a priest, shall come and atone for the matter of an elevated heart.

notes.he: מצנפת שהי' על הראש]:
notes.en: Let an item that is at a height come: the mitre, which was on the head.

messages.text: The belt atones for thought of the heart. The belt atones for the sins occurring where it is situated, i.e., over the heart, as it is written: “And you shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Tummim; and it shall be upon Aaron’s heart, when he goes in before the Lord; and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the Lord continually.”

verse.he: וְנָתַתָּ אֶל־חֹשֶׁן הַמִּשְׁפָּט אֶת־הָאוּרִים וְאֶת־הַתֻּמִּים וְהָיוּ עַל־לֵב אַהֲרֹן בְּבֹאוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְנָשָׂא אַהֲרֹן אֶת־מִשְׁפַּט בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־לִבּוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה תָּמִיד׃ {ס}
verse.en: Inside the breastpiece of decision you shall place the Urim and Thummim, so that they are over Aaron’s heart when he comes before GOD. Thus Aaron shall carry the instrument of decision for the Israelites over his heart before GOD at all times.

notes.he: אהיכא דאיתא ואבנט הוא כמו חגור של שש ארוכה מאד ואיתא נמי במדרש שהיה הכהן מקיפו סביביו ב' פעמים כנגד לב של אדם:
notes.en: The belt atones for thought of the heart, where it is: the belt is like a very long girdle of fine linen, and it is also found in the Midrash that the priest would wind it around himself twice, opposite a person’s heart.

notes.he: שכנגד לבו היה חוגרו דכתיב ולא יחגרו ביזע במקום שמזיעין כגון תחת שחיו אלא כנגד לבו שאינו מזיע שם:
notes.en: Where it is: for he would gird it opposite his heart, as it is written: “They shall not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat” (Ezekiel 44:18), [that is, not] in a place where one sweats, such as under the armpits, but opposite his heart, where one does not sweat.

messages.text: The breastplate of the High Priest atones for improper judgments, as it is written: “And you shall make a breastplate of judgment.”

verse.he: וְעָשִׂיתָ חֹשֶׁן מִשְׁפָּט מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב כְּמַעֲשֵׂה אֵפֹד תַּעֲשֶׂנּוּ זָהָב תְּכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי וְשֵׁשׁ מׇשְׁזָר תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתוֹ׃
verse.en: You shall make a breastpiece of decision, worked into a design; make it in the style of the ephod: make it of gold, of blue, purple, and crimson yarns, and of fine twisted linen.

messages.text: The ephod of the High Priest atones for idol worship, as it is written: “And without ephod or teraphim”, that is to say, when there is no ephod, the sin of teraphim, i.e., idol worship, is found. This indicates that if there is an ephod, there is no sin of idol worship.

verse.he: כִּי ׀ יָמִים רַבִּים יֵשְׁבוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין מֶלֶךְ וְאֵין שָׂר וְאֵין זֶבַח וְאֵין מַצֵּבָה וְאֵין אֵפוֹד וּתְרָפִים׃
verse.en: For the Israelites shall go a long time without king and without officials, without sacrifice and without cult pillars, and without ephod and oracle idols.

notes.he: בזמן שאין אפוד הוי עון תרפים:
notes.en: Without ephod or teraphim: at a time when there is no ephod, there is the sin of teraphim.

notes.he: כלומר אין אפוד שמכפר על עון תרפים:
notes.en: Without ephod [or teraphim]: that is to say, there is no ephod to atone for the sin of teraphim.

messages.text: The robe of the High Priest atones for malicious speech, as the Holy One, Blessed be He says: Let an item that produces sound, i.e., the bells of the robe, come and atone for an act of malicious sound, i.e., malicious speech.

notes.he: פעמוני המעיל נשמעין על מעשה קול לשון הרע ואת אמרת נגעים אתו עליה:
notes.en: That produces sound: the bells of the robe are heard, [and atone] for an act of sound, malicious speech. And you said that leprous marks come for it!

notes.he: דכתיב ונשמע קולו בבואו אלמא אית ליה כפרה לאומר לשה"ר ע"י מעיל ולא לקי בצרעת:
notes.en: An item that produces sound: as it is written: “And its sound shall be heard when he goes in” (Exodus 28:35). Evidently one who speaks malicious speech has atonement through the robe and is not struck with leprosy.

messages.text: Finally, the frontplate of the High Priest atones for an act of brazenness. From where is this derived? Here, with regard to the frontplate, it is written: “And it shall be upon Aaron’s forehead,”

verse.he: וְהָיָה עַל־מֵצַח אַהֲרֹן וְנָשָׂא אַהֲרֹן אֶת־עֲוֺן הַקֳּדָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר יַקְדִּישׁוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכׇל־מַתְּנֹת קׇדְשֵׁיהֶם וְהָיָה עַל־מִצְחוֹ תָּמִיד לְרָצוֹן לָהֶם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, that Aaron may take away any sin arising from the holy things that the Israelites consecrate, from any of their sacred donations; it shall be on his forehead at all times, to win acceptance for them before GOD.

messages.text: and there, with regard to brazenness, it is written: “And you had a prostitute’s forehead.”

verse.he: וַיִּמָּנְעוּ רְבִבִים וּמַלְקוֹשׁ לוֹא הָיָה וּמֵצַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה הָיָה לָךְ מֵאַנְתְּ הִכָּלֵם׃
verse.en:
And when showers were withheld
And the late rains did not come,
You had the brazenness of a streetwalker,
You refused to be ashamed.

messages.text: The statement of Rabbi Anani bar Sason indicates that the robe worn by the High Priest atones for malicious speech, which means that one is not punished by leprosy, as claimed by Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani.
messages.quote: The robe of the High Priest atones for malicious speech

messages.caption: Rabbi Anani bar Sason: what each of the eight priestly vestments atones for, and how the Gemara squares the tunic and the robe with the heifer and the incense.

messages.text: This is not difficult. Here, the statement of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani is referring to a case where his actions were effective and caused damage. There, Rabbi Anani bar Sason is referring to a case where his actions were not effective.

notes.he: שנתקוטטו על ידו. ואי קשיא אמאי לא מותיב ליה משפיכות דמים וגילוי עריות דקאמר לעיל נגעים באין עליהם והכא תניא דבגדי כהונה מכפרין תריץ דהא דתני בגדי כהונה מכפרין לאו עליה דידיה אלא על האחרים שעל ידו נענשין דבשפיכות דמים כתיב (במדבר ל״ה:ל״ג) כי הדם הוא יחניף וגו' ובגילוי עריות כתיב (ויקרא י״ח:כ״ה) ותטמא הארץ ואפקוד עונה עליה אבל לשון הרע לא אשכחן דמיענשי ביה אחריני:
notes.en: Where his actions were effective: that people quarreled because of him. And if you ask: why did the Gemara not object to him from bloodshed and forbidden relations, for which it said above that leprous marks come, while here it teaches that the priestly vestments atone? The answer is that this teaching, that the priestly vestments atone, is not for the sinner himself but for the others who are punished on his account. For of bloodshed it is written: “For blood pollutes [the land]” (Numbers 35:33), and of forbidden relations it is written: “And the land became impure, and I visited its iniquity upon it” (Leviticus 18:25). But with malicious speech we do not find that others are punished for it.

notes.he: פירש רש"י שנתקוטטו על ידו ואי קשיא אמאי לא מותיב ליה משפיכות דמים וגילוי עריות דקאמר לעיל נגעים באין עליהם והכא תניא דבגדי כהונה מכפרים תריץ דהא דתני בגדי כהונה מכפרי' לאו עליה דידיה אלא על אחרים דע"י שפיכות דמים נענשים העולם דכתיב (במדבר ל״ה:ל״ג) כי הדם הוא יחניף ובגילוי עריות כתיב ותטמא הארץ ואפקוד עונה עליה אבל לשון הרע לא אשכחן דאיענשי ביה אחריני לשון רש"י ולא נהירא שהרי במסכת שבועות (דף לט.) אומר דעל כל העבירות אחרים נענשים עליהם אם יש בידם למחות ואי אין בידם למחות אפי' ג"ע וש"ד נמי לא ואור"י דמשפיכות דמים לא קשיא מידי לפי שיש עליה מיתת ב"ד ובגדי כהונ' מכפרין על המיתה אבל נגעים מיהא באין עליו ועוד יש מפרש דהאי דמשני הש"ס הא דאהנו מעשיו הא דלא אהנו מעשיו קאי נמי אשפיכות דמים וגילוי עריות וה"פ אהנו מעשיו היינו כשהרג ממש ועליו אין בגדי כהונה מכפרים אלא נגעים באין עליו לא אהנו מעשיו כגון שלא הרג ממש אלא שהלבין פני חבירו ברבים דקיימא לן (ב"מ דף נח:) כל המלבין פני חבירו ברבים כאילו שופך דמים ועל זה בגדי כהונה מכפרים וכן גילוי עריות ממש אהנו מעשיו ולא אהנו מעשיו זהו כי הא דאמרי' (שבת דף נה:) מתוך ששהו קיניהן מעלה עליהם כאילו שכבום:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot quotes Rashi’s explanation in full: where his actions were effective, people quarreled because of him; and the Gemara does not raise bloodshed and forbidden relations, for which leprous marks also come, because the vestments atone for those sins only for the others punished on their account (“For blood pollutes,” Numbers 35:33; “And the land became impure, and I visited its iniquity upon it,” Leviticus 18:25), whereas for malicious speech others are not punished. Tosafot objects that this does not seem right: Shevuot 39a says that others are punished for every transgression when it was in their power to protest, and when it was not, not even for forbidden relations and bloodshed. The Ri answers that bloodshed poses no difficulty at all, since it carries a court-imposed death penalty and the priestly vestments atone for [the sin that carries] death, yet leprous marks still come upon him. Others explain that the Gemara’s answer, “where his actions were effective, where they were not effective,” applies to bloodshed and forbidden relations as well: actually killing is “effective,” and the vestments do not atone for it but leprous marks come upon him; “not effective” is, for example, shaming one’s fellow in public, which counts as shedding blood (Bava Metzia 58b), and for that the vestments atone. Likewise, actual forbidden relations are “effective,” and “not effective” is like what is said in Shabbat 55b: since they delayed the women’s bird offerings, Scripture regards them as though they had lain with them. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: If his actions were effective and caused harm or quarrels, leprous marks come upon him as punishment. If his actions were not effective and did not cause any damage, the robe atones for his sin.
But doesn’t Rabbi Simon say that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
There are two matters for which we do not find atonement through offerings, but we find atonement for them through another matter, and they are: Bloodshed and malicious speech.

With regard to bloodshed, its atonement comes from the heifer whose neck is broken. This is referring to a case where a murdered body is found but the murderer is unknown. In such an instance, the Torah mandates that the town nearest the body must break the neck of a heifer as atonement for the transgression (see Deuteronomy 21:1–9).
And malicious speech is atoned for through incense,

We have learned that incense atones, as it is written in the incident when the Israelites were afflicted with a plague for speaking slanderously against Moses and Aaron: “And he put on the incense, and made atonement for the people.”

verse.he: וַיִּקַּח אַהֲרֹן כַּאֲשֶׁר ׀ דִּבֶּר מֹשֶׁה וַיָּרׇץ אֶל־תּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל וְהִנֵּה הֵחֵל הַנֶּגֶף בָּעָם וַיִּתֵּן אֶת־הַקְּטֹרֶת וַיְכַפֵּר עַל־הָעָם׃
verse.en: Aaron took it, as Moses had ordered, and ran to the midst of the congregation, where the plague had begun among the people. He put on the incense and made expiation for the people;

messages.text: For what does incense atone? For malicious speech. It is as though the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: Let an item that is sacrificed in private, i.e., the incense, which is burnt inside the Sanctuary, come and atone for an action generally performed in private, i.e., malicious speech.
messages.lead: And similarly, the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

notes.he: קטורת נעשית בהיכל בחשאי כדתניא בפרק הוציאו לו במסכת יומא (דף מד.) פורשין מבין האולם ולמזבח בשעת הקטרה. לשון הרע בחשאי הוא:
notes.en: That is in private: the incense is offered in the Sanctuary in private, as taught in chapter Hotziu Lo of tractate Yoma (44a): they withdraw from between the Entrance Hall and the altar at the time of the burning of the incense. And malicious speech is done in private.

notes.he: קטורת שהיה עושה לפנים בהיכל (כל) שאין אדם רשאי ליכנס לשם לראותו [ויכפר על] מעשה חשאי לשה"ר שאומרים אותו [בחשאי] ובחדרי חדרים:
notes.en: Let an item that is in private come: the incense, which he would offer inside the Sanctuary, where no one is permitted to enter to see it, and let it atone for a private act, malicious speech, which people speak in private and in inner rooms.

messages.text: One statement concerning bloodshed is difficult, as it is contradicted by the other statement about bloodshed: According to Rabbi Anani bar Sason the tunic atones for bloodshed, whereas the baraita states that the heifer whose neck is broken atones for this sin.

notes.he: דקאמרינן לעיל בגדי כהונה מכפרין על אחרים וקא חזינן דעגלה ערופה מכפרת על אחרים דעל ההורג אינה מכפרת דקיימא לן בסוטה (דף מז:) שאם נתערפה העגלה ואח"כ נמצא ההורג מנין שהוא נהרג תלמוד לומר ולארץ לא יכופר וגו':
notes.en: Bloodshed is difficult, and so on: for we said above that the priestly vestments atone for others [Rashi on 16a, above], and we see that the heifer whose neck is broken atones for others, since for the killer it does not atone, as we hold in Sota (47b): if the heifer’s neck was broken and afterward the killer was found, from where do we know that he is executed? The verse states: “And no atonement can be made for the land,” and so on (Numbers 35:33).

notes.he: דהתם אמרת כתונת מכפר והכא אמרת עגלה ערופה מכפרת:
notes.en: Bloodshed is difficult with bloodshed: for there you said that the tunic atones, and here you said that the heifer whose neck is broken atones.

messages.text: Furthermore, one statement concerning malicious speech is difficult, as it is contradicted by the other statement about malicious speech: Rabbi Anani bar Sason maintains that the robe atones for malicious speech, whereas according to the baraita it is the incense that atones for this transgression.

notes.he: דלעיל דקתני דבגדי כהונה מכפרין:
notes.en: Malicious speech is difficult: with what was taught above, that the priestly vestments atone.

messages.text: The apparent contradiction between one statement about bloodshed and the other statement about bloodshed is not difficult, as this, the tunic, atones for bloodshed in a case where it is known who killed him, and that, the heifer, atones in a case where it is not known who killed him.

notes.he: עגלה מכפרת:
notes.en: Where it is not known who killed him: the heifer atones.

notes.he: כתונת מכפר:
notes.en: Where it is known who killed him: the tunic atones.

messages.text: If it is known who killed him, the murderer is deserving of death, and there is no atonement for the community until he is put to death, as the verse states: “And no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed within it, but by the blood of him that shed it.”

verse.he: וְלֹא־תַחֲנִיפוּ אֶת־הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם בָּהּ כִּי הַדָּם הוּא יַחֲנִיף אֶת־הָאָרֶץ וְלָאָרֶץ לֹא־יְכֻפַּר לַדָּם אֲשֶׁר שֻׁפַּךְ־בָּהּ כִּי־אִם בְּדַם שֹׁפְכוֹ׃
verse.en: You shall not pollute the land in which you live; for blood pollutes the land, and the land can have no expiation for blood that is shed on it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.

notes.he: וכל כמה דלא מיקטל לא מיכפרי אחריני דכתיב (במדבר ל״ה:ל״ג) ולארץ לא יכופר וגו':
notes.en: He is deserving of death: and as long as he has not been put to death, the others have no atonement, as it is written: “And no atonement can be made for the land,” and so on (Numbers 35:33).

messages.text: There are certain instances where it is impossible to put him to death, e.g., if he murdered intentionally but witnesses did not warn him beforehand of the consequences of committing murder. In such a case, the court may not put the murderer to death, as there is no punishment without prior warning.

notes.he: דלא הוה בר קטלא כתונת מכפר:
notes.en: Intentionally, but they did not warn him: so he is not liable to death; the tunic atones.

messages.text: With regard to the apparent contradiction between one statement dealing with malicious speech and the other statement about malicious speech, it is also not difficult, as this, the incense, atones for malicious speech spoken in private,

notes.he: דמעשה חשאי קטרת מכפרת:
notes.en: In private: for a private act, the incense atones.

notes.he: לשה"ר הנאמר בצנעא קטרת מכפרת דומיא דחשאי אי] דלא אהני מעשיו ממש אלא דעבד שום מילתא כגון שהלבין פני חבירו דאמרינן [מעלין עליו] כאילו הרגו או דבר ערוה כדאמרינן בבני עלי העלה הכתוב עליהן כאילו [בעלו] על כיוצא בהן מעיל מכפר:
notes.en: This in private, that in public: for malicious speech spoken in private, the incense atones, like the privacy [of the incense]. [A note in the printed edition: it seems the heading should read “That where his actions were not effective,” and so on; Rabbeinu explains that this answer applies to bloodshed as well, as Tosafot also write here in the name of “others explain.”] Where his actions were not actually effective, but he did something, for example he shamed his fellow, of whom we say it is regarded as though he killed him; or a matter of forbidden relations, as we say of the sons of Eli: Scripture regards them as though they had lain with [such women]: the robe atones.

messages.text: whereas that robe atones for malicious speech spoken in public.

notes.he: דאמעשה קול הוא מעיל מכפר:
notes.en: In public: since it is an act of sound, the robe atones.

notes.he: מעיל מכפר דומיא דנשמע קולו:
notes.en: And that, in public: the robe atones, like “and its sound shall be heard.”

messages.text: What is different and notable about a leper, that the Torah states: “He shall dwell alone; outside of the camp shall be his dwelling”?
messages.lead: asked @{rabbi-chanina}, and some say that it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Nadav, the son-in-law of Rabbi Ḥanina, who asked of Rabbi Ḥanina, and some say that he asked it of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

verse.he: כׇּל־יְמֵי אֲשֶׁר הַנֶּגַע בּוֹ יִטְמָא טָמֵא הוּא בָּדָד יֵשֵׁב מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה מוֹשָׁבוֹ׃ {ס}
verse.en: They shall be impure as long as the disease is present. Being impure, they shall dwell apart—in a dwelling outside the camp.

messages.text: By speaking malicious speech he separated between husband and wife and between one person and another; therefore he is punished with leprosy, and the Torah says: “He shall dwell alone; outside of the camp shall be his dwelling.”

notes.he: שעל לשון הרע באו נגעים עליו:
notes.en: He separated: for it was over malicious speech that leprous marks came upon him.

notes.he: שגרם להם להתקוטט על ידי לשון הרע שאמר ביניהם:
notes.en: He separated between husband and wife: for he caused them to quarrel through the malicious speech he spoke between them.

messages.text: What is different and notable about a leper that the Torah states that he is to bring two birds for his purification? The Holy One, Blessed be He says: He acted by speaking malicious speech with an act of chatter; therefore the Torah says that he is to bring an offering of birds, who chirp and chatter all the time.

verse.he: וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן וְלָקַח לַמִּטַּהֵר שְׁתֵּי־צִפֳּרִים חַיּוֹת טְהֹרוֹת וְעֵץ אֶרֶז וּשְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת וְאֵזֹב׃
verse.en: the priest shall order two live pure birds, cedar wood, crimson stuff, and hyssop to be brought for the one to be purified.

notes.he: לשון קול היוצא בחשאי ובלע"ז פולי"ר:
notes.en: Chatter [patit]: a word for a sound that goes out quietly; (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: שהצפרים צועקין בכל שעה:
notes.en: He is to bring an offering of chatter: for birds cry out all the time.

notes.he: פיטפט והשמיע קולו בלשון הרע:
notes.en: An act of chatter: he chattered and made his voice heard in malicious speech.

notes.he: ציפורין שמשמיעין קול בכל שעה]:
notes.en: Therefore he is to bring an offering of chatter: birds, which make their voices heard all the time.

messages.text: “You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall rebuke [hokhe’aḥ tokhiaḥ] your neighbor, and do not bear sin because of him.” Why does the verse specify “in your heart”? One might have thought that the verse means: Do not hit him, do not slap him, and do not ruin him due to hatred. Therefore the verse states “in your heart.” This teaches that the verse speaks of hatred in the heart.

verse.he: לֹא־תִשְׂנָא אֶת־אָחִיךָ בִּלְבָבֶךָ הוֹכֵחַ תּוֹכִיחַ אֶת־עֲמִיתֶךָ וְלֹא־תִשָּׂא עָלָיו חֵטְא׃
verse.en: You shall not hate your kinsfolk in your heart. Reprove your kindred but uncertain. incur no guilt on their account.

notes.he: על דבר תוכחה:
notes.en: One might have thought: do not hit him: over a matter that calls for rebuke.

notes.he: כלאחר יד:
notes.en: Slap him: with the back of the hand.

notes.he: דהיינו (הוא) לא תשנא שלא יכנו כו':
notes.en: One might have thought: that is, that “You shall not hate” means that he should not hit him, and so on.

messages.text: From where is it derived with regard to one who sees an unseemly matter in another that he is obligated to rebuke him? As it is stated: “You shall rebuke [hokhe’aḥ tokhiaḥ] your neighbor.”

If one rebuked him for his action but he did not accept the rebuke, from where is it derived that he must rebuke him again? The verse states: “You shall rebuke [hokhe’aḥ tokhiaḥ],” and the double language indicates he must rebuke in any case.

One might have thought that one should continue rebuking him even if his face changes due to humiliation. Therefore, the verse states: “Do not bear sin because of him”; the one giving rebuke may not sin by embarrassing the other person.

notes.he: שיוכיחנו ברבים להלבין פניו:
notes.en: And his face changes: that he rebukes him in public, so as to make his face blanch.

notes.he: של מתוכח כגון שמוכיחו בפני רבים]:
notes.en: One might have thought, even if his face changes: the face of the one rebuked, for example if he rebukes him in front of many.

notes.he: שלא תביישנו:
notes.en: Do not bear sin because of him: that you not shame him.

messages.text: I would be surprised if there is anyone in this generation who can receive rebuke. Why? Because if the one rebuking says to him: Remove the splinter from between your eyes, i.e., rid yourself of a minor infraction, the other says to him: Remove the beam from between your eyes, i.e., you have committed far more severe sins.

notes.he: כלומר עון קטן שבידך זה יכול לומר לו טול אתה עון גדול שבידך הלכך אין יכולין להוכיח שכולן חוטאים:
notes.en: Splinter: that is to say, [if one says to him: remove] the small sin in your hand, this one can say to him: Remove, you, the great sin in your hand. Therefore they cannot rebuke, since they are all sinners.

notes.dh: [אם יש בדור הזה מי שיכול להוכיח
notes.he: כלומר שאפילו הטובים מקלקלין מעשיהן ואינן יכולין להוכיח אחרים שאם יאמר לחברו טול קיסם מבין (עיניך) [שיניך] יכול להשיבו טול קורה מבין (שיניך) [עיניך]:
notes.en: If there is anyone in this generation who can rebuke: that is to say, even the good ones spoil their deeds and cannot rebuke others; for if one says to his fellow, “Remove the splinter from between your teeth” [the printed text is corrected here from “eyes”], he can answer him, “Remove the beam from between your eyes.”

notes.he: שאם מוכיחין בדור הזה לאדם מיד שונאו:
notes.en: Who can receive rebuke: for if, in this generation, one rebukes a person, he immediately hates him.

messages.text: I would be surprised if there is anyone in this generation who knows how to rebuke correctly, without embarrassing the person he is rebuking.

notes.he: דרך כבוד שלא יהו פניו משתנין:
notes.en: Who knows how to rebuke: respectfully, so that his face does not change.

notes.he: שיודע להוכיח כגון שלא יהו פניו של מתוכח משתנים]:
notes.en: Who knows how to rebuke: for example, so that the face of the one rebuked does not change.

messages.text: I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses before me that Akiva was lashed, i.e., punished, many times on my account, as I would complain about him before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Great. And all the more so I thereby increased his love for me.

notes.he: כשהייתי רואה בו דבר גנאי:
notes.en: I would complain about him: when I saw something unseemly in him.

messages.text: This incident serves to affirm that which is stated: “Do not rebuke a scorner lest he hate you; rebuke a wise man and he will love you.” A wise man wants to improve himself and loves those who assist him in that task.

verse.he: אַל־תּוֹכַח לֵץ פֶּן־יִשְׂנָאֶךָּ הוֹכַח לְחָכָם וְיֶאֱהָבֶךָּ׃
verse.en:
Do not rebuke scoffers, for they will hate you;
Reprove the wise, and they will love you.

messages.text: If one is faced with the choice of rebuke for its own sake, or humility not for its own sake, which of them is preferable?

notes.he: לשם שמים:
notes.en: Rebuke for its own sake: for the sake of Heaven.

notes.he: שעושה עצמו עניו שאינו רוצה להוכיחו ואותה ענוה שלא לשם שמים הוא אלא שלא ישנאנו:
notes.en: And humility not for its own sake: that he makes himself humble and does not want to rebuke him, and that humility is not for the sake of Heaven but so that the other will not hate him.

notes.he: שעושה עצמו עניו ואינו רוצה להוכיחו ואותה ענוה לא לשם שמים היא אלא שלא ישנאנו וי"מ ענוה שלא לשמה פירוש משום גאוה או שיאמרו אדם עניו הוא ומשפיל עצמו ושותק בחירופו ועלבונו ולא לשם שמים אלא לקנות שם אבל בקונט' שפירש ענוה שלא לשמה שמונע תוכחה מן הצריכים לא ישר אלי דהוה רשע גמור:
notes.en: And humility not for its own sake: that he makes himself humble and does not want to rebuke him, and that humility is not for the sake of Heaven but so that the other will not hate him. And some explain humility not for its own sake as [humility] out of pride, or so that people will say, “He is a humble man, who lowers himself and stays silent when he is reviled and insulted,” not for the sake of Heaven but to make a name for himself. But the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained humility not for its own sake as withholding rebuke from those who need it, does not seem right to me, for that is a completely wicked person.

messages.text: Do you not concede that humility for its own sake is preferable? As the Master says: Humility is the greatest of all the positive attributes. If so, humility not for its own sake is also preferable, as Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:

notes.he: במסכת עבודה זרה בפ"ק (דף כ:) ענוה גדולה מכולן דכתיב יען משח אותי לבשר ענוים לבשר חסידים לא נאמר:
notes.en: As the Master says: in the first chapter of tractate Avoda Zara (20b): Humility is the greatest of them all, as it is written: “Because the Lord has anointed me to bring good tidings to the humble” (Isaiah 61:1); it does not say “to the pious.”

notes.he: דתניא במס' (כתובות) [ע"ז] (דף כ) רבי (נחום) אומר זריזות מביאה לידי נקיות כו' עד ענוה גדולה מכולם דכתיב רוח ה' עלי וגו':
notes.en: As the Master says: Humility is the greatest of them all: as taught in tractate Avoda Zara (20b) [the printed text corrects “Ketubot”]: Rabbi [a name, “Naḥum,” is marked for deletion] says: Alacrity brings one to cleanliness, and so on, up to: humility is the greatest of them all, as it is written: “The spirit of the Lord is upon me,” and so on.

messages.text: A person should always engage in Torah and mitzvot even if not for their own sake, i.e., without the proper motivation but for ulterior motives, as through the performance of mitzvot not for their own sake, one will come in the end to do them for their own sake.
What is considered rebuke for its own sake and humility not for its own sake? It is like this incident that occurred when Rav Huna and Ḥiyya bar Rav were sitting before Shmuel.
messages.quote: rebuke for its own sake, or humility not for its own sake

messages.text: @Shmuel See, Master, that Rav Huna is afflicting me.

notes.he: לשמואל חזי מר דקא מצער לן רב הונא שמכה וחובט אותי:
notes.en: [Ḥiyya bar Rav] said to him [Rashi’s heading reads “Rabbi Ḥiyya”]: to Shmuel: “See, Master, that Rav Huna is distressing us,” in that he strikes and beats me.

messages.text: Rav Huna accepted upon himself that he would not afflict Ḥiyya bar Rav anymore. After Ḥiyya bar Rav left,

notes.he: חייא בר רב:
notes.en: After he left: Ḥiyya bar Rav.

messages.text: @Shmuel Ḥiyya bar Rav did such-and-such to me, and therefore I was in the right to cause him distress.

notes.he: חייא בר רב אמר ליה רב הונא לשמואל להכי מצערנא ליה דהכי והכי עביד דברים מגונים והיינו ענוה שלא לשמה דלא אמר ליה בפניו ושלא בפניו סיפר בגנותו:
notes.en: When he left: when Ḥiyya bar Rav left, Rav Huna said to Shmuel: This is why I distress him, because he does such-and-such disgraceful things. And this is humility not for its own sake, for he did not say it to his face, and behind his back he spoke of his disgrace.

notes.he: רב הונא לשמואל הכי הוה עביד לי]:
notes.en: He said to him: Rav Huna said to Shmuel: This is what he was doing to me.

messages.text: @Rav Huna Why did you not say this in his presence?
Heaven forbid that the son of Rav should be humiliated because of me.

notes.dh: חס ליה דליכסוף זרעיה דרב על ידאי
notes.he: וזהו ענוה שלא לשמה שהניחו לביישו משום כבוד אביו:
notes.en: Heaven forbid that the seed of Rav should be humiliated because of me: and this is humility not for its own sake, for he refrained from shaming him because of his father’s honor.

notes.dh: חס לי דליכסף זרעיה דרב על ידאי
notes.he: וזו היא ענוה שלא לשמה שמוטב היה שאמרה בפניו כדי שיוכיחנו והיא היתה תוכחה לשמה ממה שלא אמרה בפניו ואמר לאחריו:
notes.en: Heaven forbid that the seed of Rav should be humiliated because of me: and this is humility not for its own sake. For it would have been better had he said it to his face, in order to rebuke him, and that would have been rebuke for its own sake, than not saying it to his face and saying it behind him.

messages.text: This provides an example of rebuke for its own sake, as Rav Huna originally rebuked Ḥiyya bar Rav only when Shmuel was not present, and of humility not for its own sake, as Rav Huna did not forgive Ḥiyya bar Rav but simply did not wish to humiliate him.
§ Until where does the obligation of rebuke extend?

notes.he: אדם חייב להוכיח את חבירו:
notes.en: Until where: is a person obligated to rebuke his fellow?

notes.he: עד היכן חייב שלא ימנע מלהוכיח את חברו]:
notes.en: Until where is rebuke: that is, up to what point is he obligated not to refrain from rebuking his fellow?

messages.text: Until his rebuke is met by hitting, i.e., until the person being rebuked hits the person rebuking him.

notes.he: עד שיקצוף זה ויכה את המוכיח:
notes.en: Until hitting: until this one grows angry and hits the one rebuking.

notes.he: עד שיכנו המתוכח לומר איני חפץ בתוכחתך:
notes.en: Until hitting: until the one rebuked hits him, as if to say: I do not want your rebuke.

messages.text: Until his rebuke is met by cursing, i.e., he curses the one rebuking him.

notes.he:
שיקלל את המוכיח:
יהונתן הוכיח לשאול עד שקצף שאול:
notes.en: Until cursing: until he curses the one rebuking. Jonathan rebuked Saul until Saul grew angry.

notes.he: [או] עד שיקללנו המתוכח:
notes.en: Until cursing: or until the one rebuked curses him.

messages.text: Until his rebuke is met by reprimand.

notes.he: עד שיגער בו המתוכח:
notes.en: Or until reprimand: until the one rebuked scolds him.

messages.text: This dispute between these amora’im is like a dispute between tanna’im:
Until his rebuke is met by hitting;
Until his rebuke is met by cursing;
Until his rebuke is met by reprimand.

And all three of them expounded the same one verse, from which they derived their respective opinions. After Jonathan rebuked his father, Saul, for the way he treated David, the verse states: “Then Saul’s anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said unto him: You son of perverse rebellion, do not I know that you have chosen the son of Yishai to your own shame, and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness.”

verse.he: וַיִּחַר־אַף שָׁאוּל בִּיהוֹנָתָן וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ בֶּן־נַעֲוַת הַמַּרְדּוּת הֲלוֹא יָדַעְתִּי כִּי־בֹחֵר אַתָּה לְבֶן־יִשַׁי לְבׇשְׁתְּךָ וּלְבֹשֶׁת עֶרְוַת אִמֶּךָ׃
verse.en: Saul flew into a rage against Jonathan. “You son of a perverse, rebellious woman!” he shouted. “I know that you side with the son of Jesse—to your shame, and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness!

notes.he: שאול היה המתוכח ויונתן המוכיח:
notes.en: Then Saul’s anger was kindled: Saul was the one rebuked and Jonathan the one rebuking.

messages.text: And it is written: “And Saul cast his spear at him to smite him, whereby Jonathan knew that it had been determined by his father to put David to death.”

verse.he: וַיָּטֶל שָׁאוּל אֶת־הַחֲנִית עָלָיו לְהַכֹּתוֹ וַיֵּדַע יְהוֹנָתָן כִּי־כָלָה הִיא מֵעִם אָבִיו לְהָמִית אֶת־דָּוִד׃ {ס}
verse.en: At that, Saul threw his spear at him to strike him down; and Jonathan realized that his father was determined to do away with David.

messages.text: According to the one who says: Until his rebuke is met by hitting, it is derived from that which is written: “To smite him.”
And according to the one who says: Until his rebuke is met by cursing, it is derived from that which is written: “To the shame of your mother’s nakedness.”
And according to the one who says: Until his rebuke is met by reprimand, it is derived from that which is written: “Then Saul’s anger was kindled.”

notes.he: ויחר אף שאול היינו נזיפה שנזף בו:
notes.en: Then Saul’s anger was kindled: that is reprimand, for he reprimanded him.

messages.text: But according to the one who says: Until his rebuke is met by reprimand, aren’t both hitting and cursing written in that verse?
messages.quote: Until his rebuke is met by reprimand

notes.dh: ומאן דאמר עד נזיפה הא כתיב הכאה וקללה
notes.he: ואם תאמר למאן דאמר נמי קללה הא כתיב הכאה וי"ל שמא כדמשני אגב חביבותא דיונתן אי נמי לא דריש ליה קרא דויטל שאול כיון דליתיה בהאי קרא דויחר אף שאול אלא קרא אחרינא הוא:
notes.en: But according to the one who says: Until reprimand, aren’t hitting and cursing written? And if you say: according to the one who says cursing, too, isn’t hitting written? One can say: perhaps as the Gemara answers, it was due to Jonathan’s fondness [for David]. Alternatively, he does not expound the verse “And Saul cast,” since it is not part of this verse, “Then Saul’s anger was kindled,” but is a different verse.

messages.text: It is different there, as due to the special fondness that Jonathan had for David, he subjected himself to more abuse than is required by halakha.

notes.he: שהיה פטור מלהוכיחו משעה שנזף בו:
notes.en: He subjected himself to more: for he was exempt from rebuking him from the moment [Saul] reprimanded him.

messages.caption: How far must one keep rebuking? Three Amoraim, three Tannaim, and the words of one verse about Saul and Jonathan.

messages.text: Apropos the topic of losing patience and hitting another: Until where does the requirement that a person should not change his place of lodging extend, i.e., how much must one suffer before he may move elsewhere?

notes.dh: עד היכן לא ישנה אדם מאכסניא שלו
notes.he: כלומר עד כמה צריך האכסנאי לסבול מבעה"ב שלו ולא יצא מביתו:
notes.en: Until where should a person not change his lodging: that is, how much must the guest bear from his host before leaving his house?

messages.text: Until the point of the host’s hitting him.

notes.he: בעל הבית את האכסנאי או את אשתו:
notes.en: Until hitting: the host hits the guest or his wife.

notes.he: [עד] שיכנו בעל הבית לומר צא מביתי:
notes.en: Until hitting: until the host hits him, as if to say: Leave my house.

messages.text: Until the host packs up the guest’s clothes and places them on his back to throw him out.

notes.he: בעל הבית כלי האכסנאי לאחוריו להשליכם מן הבית:
notes.en: Until he packs: the host packs the guest’s things on his back, to throw them out of the house.

notes.he: שיניח לו כליו על מקלו ויתנם על צוארו להוציאו מביתו:
notes.en: Until he packs his things on his back: that he puts his things on his staff and places them on his neck, to put him out of his house.

messages.text: If it is a case where the host hits the guest himself, everyone agrees that the guest may move lodging. Similarly, if the host packs up the guest’s clothes and places them on his back, everyone also agrees that he may leave.

notes.he: אם יכה את האכסנאי עצמו כולי עלמא לא פליגי דודאי יש לו לצאת:
notes.en: With hitting him himself: if he hits the guest himself, everyone agrees that he certainly may leave.

messages.text: When they disagree is in a case where the host hits his wife. One Sage, Rav, holds that since the host does not hurt the guest himself, what difference does it make to him? Therefore, he should not change his lodging on that account. And one Sage, Shmuel, holds that if he continues to stay in that place he will come to fight with his host about this matter.

notes.he: בהפשלה ובהכאה דאכסנאי גופיה כ"ע לא פליגי דתו לא מצי קאי: שמואל סבר כיון דלדידיה אינו מכה מאי נפקא ליה מיניה הלכך עד הפשלה:
notes.en: With packing, and with hitting the guest himself, everyone agrees that he can no longer stay. Shmuel holds: since he does not hit him himself, what difference does it make to him? Therefore [he stays] until packing. [Rashi thus gives this reason to Shmuel; the English on the daf gives it to Rav.]

notes.he: להתקוטט:
notes.en: Come to fight [le’itrodei]: to quarrel.

notes.he: של אכסנאי:
notes.en: Hitting his wife: the guest’s wife.

notes.he: להתקוטט עם בעל הבית מפני מה הכה את אשתו:
notes.en: He will come to fight: to quarrel with the host over why he hit his wife.

messages.text: The Aramaic says only “one Sage holds … and one Sage holds.” The English names Rav for the first reason and Shmuel for the second; Rashi assigns them the other way around (see the notes).

And why is it so important that one should remain in the same lodging until he is forced to leave? It is as the Master says: A guest has the potential to degrade and to be degraded. If he moves from one place of lodging to another, people will assume that his host is unpleasant to him and that he is not a well-behaved guest, as the two of them cannot get along with one another, and the reputations of both of them will be tarnished.

notes.he: לו לסבול:
notes.en: And why is it so: [why must] he bear so much?

notes.he: המשנה מאכסניא שלו:
notes.en: A guest: who changes his lodging.

notes.he: בעל הבית:
notes.en: Degrades: the host.

notes.he: הוא עצמו דאמרי אינשי כמה קשים אלו שלא יוכלו לדור יחד:
notes.en: And is degraded: himself, for people say: How difficult these two are, that they could not live together.

notes.he: כלומר למה יש לו לסבול כ"כ קודם שיצא:
notes.en: And why is it so: that is, why must he bear so much before he leaves?

notes.he: [אם ישנה אכסניא שלו] יאמרו מכוער הוא בעה"ב שלא היה יכול לסובלו וגם את האכסנאי [יפגמו ויאמרו] מכוער היה שלא סבל את בעה"ב:
notes.en: As the Master says: A guest degrades and is degraded: if he changes his lodging, people will say the host is unpleasant, since the guest could not bear him; and they will also degrade the guest and say he was unpleasant, since he did not bear with the host.

messages.text: From where in the Torah is it derived that a person should not change his place of lodging? As it is stated when Abraham returned from Egypt: “And he went on his journeys from the South to Beth El, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Beth El and Ai.” Abraham took pains to revisit the same places he had stayed on his journey to Egypt.

verse.he: וַיֵּלֶךְ לְמַסָּעָיו מִנֶּגֶב וְעַד־בֵּית־אֵל עַד־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־הָיָה שָׁם אׇהֳלֹה בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בֵּית־אֵל וּבֵין הָעָי׃
verse.en: And he proceeded by stages from the Negeb as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been formerly, between Bethel and Ai,

notes.dh: עד המקום אשר היה שם אהלו
notes.he: מכאן שחזר לאכסנאי שהיה בה בתחלה:
notes.en: To the place where his tent had been: from here [we learn] that he returned to the lodging he had been in at first.

messages.text: The source is from here, the beginning of the verse: “And he went on his journeys,” i.e., the same journeys he made on the way down to Egypt.

notes.he: בדרך שהיה רגיל לחנות ממסע למסע שלא שינה בית מלוניו:
notes.en: On his journeys: on the road where he used to camp from journey to journey, for he did not change his lodging places.

notes.he: לאותן מסעות שהלך תחלה:
notes.en: And he went on his journeys: on those journeys he had gone on at first.

messages.text: What is the difference between these two explanations? The practical difference between them is with regard to a temporary lodging. According to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina, even one who is on a journey must return to stay in the same place where he originally lodged, whereas “his tent” indicates a measure of permanence.

notes.he: כגון אכסנאי שבדרך שלן שם במקרה בעלמא ששקעה לו שם חמה. למאן דאמר מאהלו לא חשיב אלא אכסניא קבועה ומאן דאמר ממסעיו חשיב אפילו דאקראי:
notes.en: A temporary lodging: for example, a guest on the road who lodged there merely by chance, because the sun set on him there. According to the one who says “his tent,” only a fixed lodging counts; according to the one who says “his journeys,” even a temporary one counts.

notes.he: שאין אדם רגיל שם אלא לפי שעה נזדמנה לו אם צריך לקבוע שם למאן דאמר למסעיו [למסעות] תדירות אבל דאקראי לא:
notes.en: A temporary lodging: where a person does not regularly stay, but it happened to him for the moment: [the question is] whether he must make it his fixed lodging. According to the one who says “his journeys,” [this means] regular journeys, but not a temporary one. [Rashi reads the difference the other way.]

messages.text: From where is it derived that a person should not change from his craft and from the craft of his fathers? As it is stated: “And King Solomon sent and fetched Hiram out of Tyre. He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass; and he was filled with wisdom and understanding and skill, to work all works in brass. And he came to King Solomon, and wrought all his work.”

verse.he: וַיִּשְׁלַח הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה וַיִּקַּח אֶת־חִירָם מִצֹּר׃ בֶּן־אִשָּׁה אַלְמָנָה הוּא מִמַּטֵּה נַפְתָּלִי וְאָבִיו אִישׁ־צֹרִי חֹרֵשׁ נְחֹשֶׁת וַיִּמָּלֵא אֶת־הַחׇכְמָה וְאֶת־הַתְּבוּנָה וְאֶת־הַדַּעַת לַעֲשׂוֹת כׇּל־מְלָאכָה בַּנְּחֹשֶׁת וַיָּבוֹא אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה וַיַּעַשׂ אֶת־כׇּל־מְלַאכְתּוֹ׃
verse.en: King Solomon sent for Hiram and brought him down from Tyre. He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a Tyrian, a coppersmith. He was endowed with skill, ability, and talent for executing all work in bronze. denotes both copper and bronze. In the translation “copper” is ordinarily used for the natural product and “bronze” for the artifacts. He came to King Solomon and executed all his work.

notes.dh: (לעיל) לעולם אל ישנה אדם מאומנות אביו ומאומנות אבותיו
notes.he: ומייתי ראיה שאמו היתה מבני דן ולקח לו אומנות אבותיו:
notes.en: A person should never change from the craft of his father and the craft of his fathers: and it brings a proof that his mother was of the children of Dan, and he took up for himself the craft of his forefathers.

notes.he: במלכים כתיב. וכתיב בדברי הימים בן אשה וגו' דאבוה דאימיה היה מדן אלמא שהחזיק):
notes.en: “And King Solomon sent”: this is written in Kings. And in Chronicles it is written: “The son of a woman,” and so on, for his mother’s father was from Dan; evidently he held on [to the craft of his fathers].

messages.text: And the Master says: Hiram’s mother was also from the house of Dan, as the verse states about him: “The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan” (II Chronicles 2:13).

notes.he: הכי גרסינן דאמר מר אימיה מדן ואבוה מנפתלי דבדברי הימים (ב ב) כתיב ואמו מבני דן:
notes.en: This is how we read it: “As the Master says: His mother was from Dan and his father from Naphtali,” for in Chronicles (II Chronicles 2) it is written that his mother was of the children of Dan.

messages.text: And it is written with regard to those who constructed the Tabernacle: “And with him was Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman, and a skillful workman, and a weaver in colors, in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and fine linen.” This teaches that Hiram continued in the craft of brass work, the craft of his father’s family and also of his mother’s family from Dan.

verse.he: וְאִתּוֹ אׇהֳלִיאָב בֶּן־אֲחִיסָמָךְ לְמַטֵּה־דָן חָרָשׁ וְחֹשֵׁב וְרֹקֵם בַּתְּכֵלֶת וּבָאַרְגָּמָן וּבְתוֹלַעַת הַשָּׁנִי וּבַשֵּׁשׁ׃ {ס}
verse.en: at his side was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, carver and designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and crimson yarns and in fine linen.

notes.he: [ואביו היה ממטה נפתלי ואימיה דאבוה מדן דכתיב בדברי הימים בן אשה מבנות דן הוא והחזיק] באומנות אבותיו מאביו ומאמו:
notes.en: And his father was of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father’s mother was from Dan, as it is written in Chronicles: “The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan.” And he held on to the craft of his fathers, from his father’s side and his mother’s.

messages.text: § Until where is the minimum limit of suffering? What is the least amount pain that is included in the definition of suffering?

notes.he: סוף מדת יסורין כלומר יסורין שאין פחותין מהן:
notes.en: The limit of suffering: the end of the measure of suffering, that is, suffering than which there is none smaller.

notes.he: כלומר עד כמה צער קטן יחשב יסורין שאם יארע לו בתוך ארבעים יום שיהא לו כפרה ולא קבל בכאן עולמו:
notes.en: Until where is the limit of suffering: that is, how small a distress counts as suffering, so that if it happens to him within forty days he has atonement and has not received his World here.

messages.text: Anyone for whom they wove a garment to wear and the garment does not suit him, i.e., it does not fit him exactly.

notes.he: שאינו למדתו כהגון וצער הוא לו:
notes.en: And it does not suit him: it is not made to his measure properly, and it is a distress to him.

notes.he: שאינו למדת גופו או קטן או גדול הרי אלו (יסוריו) [יסורין]:
notes.en: And it does not suit him: it is not the size of his body, either too small or too large; this is suffering.

messages.text: The Sages said an even greater statement than this, i.e., that even lesser inconvenience is still considered suffering: Even if people intended that they would dilute his wine with hot water, but they accidentally diluted it for him with cold water, it is considered suffering. Similarly, if he wanted it diluted with cold water, but they diluted it for him with hot water, this too is considered suffering. And you say all this, that it is considered suffering, only if the garment one ordered does not fit?
messages.lead: Rava the Younger objects to this, and some say Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani objects:
messages.quote: they wove a garment to wear and the garment does not suit him

notes.he: כוס של יין במים חמין:
notes.en: To dilute: a cup of wine with hot water.

messages.text: Even if one’s cloak turns around as he puts it on, so that he has to take it off and put it on again, this too is considered a form of suffering.

notes.he: שלא לבשה כסדר וצריך להופכה ולפושטה:
notes.en: His cloak turns around: he did not put it on in the right way, and he must turn it over and take it off.

notes.he: בשעה שהיה מבקש ללובשו:
notes.en: His cloak turns around: at the moment he sought to put it on.

messages.alt: and some say Rav Ḥisda, and some say Rabbi Yitzḥak, and some say it was taught in a baraita
messages.text: Even if one reached his hand into his pocket to take out three coins, but two coins came up in his hand, it is considered a form of suffering.

notes.he: שצריך עוד לטרוח להושיט ידו פעם שניה ליקח שלישי]:
notes.en: To take three, and two came up: for he must take more trouble and reach his hand in a second time to take the third.

messages.text: It constitutes suffering specifically in a case where one reached into his pocket to take three coins, and two coins came up in his hand. But if he reached into his pocket to take two, and instead three coins came up in his hand, this is not considered to be suffering, as it is not an exertion to drop the extra coin back into his pocket.

notes.he: איכא טירחא למיהדר ולמשקל שלישית:
notes.en: Three, and two came up in his hand: there is the exertion of going back and taking a third.

messages.text: And why is it so important to know the least amount of suffering? As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught in a baraita:

notes.he: כלומר למאי הילכתא הוו יסורין:
notes.en: And why is it so: that is, for what halakhic purpose do we need to know what counts as suffering?

notes.he: [למה] לי למידק עד היכן תכלית יסורין:
notes.en: And why is it so: why do I need to be precise about the limit of suffering?

messages.text: Anyone who passes forty days without suffering has received his World, i.e., his reward, and he will have no further reward in the World-to-Come.

notes.he: כל מנוחתו לעתיד ואי עבר עליה חד מהנך הרי הוא יסורין:
notes.en: Has received his World: all his repose that awaits him in the future [he has received here]. And if one of these things happens to him, that is suffering.

messages.text: In the West, Eretz Yisrael, they say:
Continues on 17a: in the West they say of one who passes forty days without suffering, “A calamity awaits him.” The Gemara then returns to the topic of rebuke.
